flashcard_questions.q: Who was the Ancient Greek physician called the 'Father of Medicine'?
Hippocrates lived from about 460 to ____ BC.
What did Hippocrates argue caused disease, against the common Greek view?
flashcard_questions.a: Natural causes rather than the gods.

flashcard_questions.q: Which humour was linked to winter, water, and a cold and wet nature?
Which humour was linked to summer, fire, and a hot and dry nature?
Which humour was linked to autumn, earth, and a cold and dry nature?
Which collection of medical texts did Hippocrates and his followers compile?
Which set of ethical rules for doctors is attributed to Hippocrates?
Who was the Roman physician who developed the Theory of Opposites?
How long did Galen work as a doctor at a gladiator school?
How did Galen prove the brain, not the heart, controlled the body?
flashcard_questions.a: By cutting a pig's spinal cord at different points.

flashcard_questions.q: How many books did Galen write?
Under the Theory of Opposites, how would a fever be treated?
What treatment was used for an excess of black bile?
Why did the Church promote Galen's work so strongly?
flashcard_questions.a: His idea of a perfectly designed body fitted Christian belief in creation.

notes: 15 cards: 4 term-to-definition, 4 person-to-significance, 3 humour-to-quality, 2 cause-effect, 1 figure, 1 cloze. Left blood out of the humour set to keep three uniquely identifying fronts.
